findings.issue_text: Scope caveat:** this checkout is a sparse tree of only the 22 changed files — no `schema.prisma`, no `node_modules`, no other app-store calendar services. `tsc` cannot run, so repo-wide claims are bounded by those 22 files. I've flagged the items where that limits verification.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — TODO left in task-done diff ("// TODO: i18n this string?"). VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: the diff only changes "organiser"→"organizer" on that line; the marker is untouched. Gate false positive in substance.
Manifest blocker: "missing shard result for shard-01" — no reviewer output was recorded for the single shard covering all 23 paths; scaffold verdict NEEDS_REVISION.
PASS (0 blocking) — contradicted by the security lens below; the gate did not detect the removed credential-ownership checks.
PASS (0 blocking) — contradicted by the completeness lens; the only test-side change is one Playwright fixture line.
PASS (0 blocking) — contradicted by the architecture lens below.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 — optional chaining dropped: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no `?.`. Empty/null is the normal case (handleNewBooking.ts:1066 emits `null`; confirm/cancel/webhook handlers emit `[]`), so a Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws TypeError — the branch crashes in precisely the "Google Meet w/o Google Cal" case it exists to handle. VERIFIED: no try/catch wraps eventManager.create (try at 1951 closes at 1991; call at 2114), while createBooking already ran at 1952 → 500 plus an orphaned ACCEPTED booking row with zero references, no emails, no webhooks.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-166 — CalDAV/Apple base: per-host call filters host B's calendar list by host A's externalId → `[]` → `Promise.all([])` → `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false → returns SUCCESS with a uid having created nothing. VERIFIED by reading lines 150-190. Silent false success; a booking reference is persisted for an event that does not exist.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:71-76, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125-131, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — three of four Calendar implementations still resolve `destinationCalendar[0]` and ignore the new `credentialId` param. TypeScript will NOT flag this (fewer params are assignable), so `implements Calendar` still compiles. Multi-host is delivered for Google only; O365/Lark send host A's externalId under host B's token → 404, swallowed as success:false at CalendarManager.ts:236-240.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 and :315-317 — tautological lookup: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. The find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares against undefined and can never match. Replaced a working `destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. updateEvent now sends calendarId:undefined; deleteEvent falls through to "primary" → cancelled/rescheduled events are never removed from the real calendar.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when the base value is `null` (line 1063-1067: neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar). Every co-host calendar collected at 992-993 is discarded with no log or error — the exact configuration this task targets fails quietly. This is also the only site in the diff emitting `null` rather than `[]`, which is what makes the EventManager.ts:118 crash reachable.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — condition INVERTED in a file unrelated to this task: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Line 153's rewrite IS behavior-preserving, which marks 151 as an accidental flip. Billing on → the org slug is claimed at creation before payment with isOrganizationVerified:false; billing off (self-hosted) → the org gets neither slug nor requestedSlug and is unroutable.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` (was `: result.credentialId`). The video branch now always stores undefined. VERIFIED consumer at handleCancelBooking.ts:491: `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)` with no else — so cancelling a booking created after this deploy never deletes the Zoom/Teams/Daily meeting. Unrelated to destinationCalendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208-209 — updateLocation's referencesToCreate reads `result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`, but VERIFIED that CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 312-322) returns neither field; only createEvent sets them. editLocation.handler.ts persists these via `references: { create: ... }`, so every location edit writes calendar references with both routing keys null, degrading later cancel/reschedule to the legacy fan-out path.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175-179, packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:119/229, paypal-webhook.ts:152-156 — these rebuild a strictly one-element array from the single `booking.destinationCalendar` relation. VERIFIED that handleNewBooking.ts:2114 calls eventManager.create only under `!requiresConfirmation && !paymentAppData.price`. Consequence: collective events that require confirmation or payment still write to exactly one calendar — the feature works only on the instant-confirm, unpaid path.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1874-1877 — only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected; Booking.destinationCalendar stays 1:1. The multi-destination array exists only in memory for one request and can never be reconstructed by any later read path.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-154 with packages/core/EventManager.ts:375-382 — matching solely on `cal.credentialId === credentialId` while DestinationCalendar.credentialId is nullable (the code branches on it at EventManager.ts:340/375). In the null branch `createEvent(c, event)` is called with no externalId, the find cannot match, and `selectedCalendar || "primary"` sends booking PII (attendee names/emails, notes, custom-input responses) to the user's primary calendar instead of the one they chose. No migration/backfill in the diff.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — the hangout-link `events.patch` still uses bare `selectedCalendar` while the insert at :154 was defended with `|| "primary"`. VERIFIED: patch can fire with calendarId:undefined on an unawaited, uncaught promise.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:511-541 — the security lens reported `credential` leaking across loop iterations; VERIFIED INCORRECT — `credential` is reassigned unconditionally at line 512. The real defect: when the DB fetch returns nothing OR returns a credential whose `app.slug` is falsy, `credential` stays undefined and is passed to `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which dereferences `credential.appName`. VERIFIED that line 590 is `return Promise.all(result)` — NOT awaited — so the rejection escapes the local catch at 591 and propagates out of reschedule() as a 500.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — reschedule-merge still uses `.find()` on calendar references while the surrounding code was converted to `.filter()`. Hosts 2..N keep stale duplicate events at the old time slot.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:454 — the inner `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` was left singular. Cancelling a recurring collective series deletes only the first host's event from each remaining occurrence.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344-355, :517-528, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433-441 — three unscoped `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` calls. Previously the code could only act with credentials in `this.calendarCredentials` (constructed from ONE user) or `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` — an implicit ownership boundary that failed closed. Now any credentialId reachable from a DestinationCalendar or BookingReference row is loaded with its encrypted key and used, with no userId/teamId predicate. `credentialFromDB.invalid` is copied at :364 but never checked, and these credentials bypass the refreshCredentials() pass. Exploitability end-to-end depends on setDestinationCalendar input validation, which is NOT in this checkout — the missing authorization check itself is fully verifiable here.

Public webhook contract broken with no versioning — handleNewBooking.ts:1754/2296 spread `...evt` into webhookData, so destinationCalendar is serialized to subscribers. VERIFIED inconsistent fixtures in apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts: `null` at :119 and :373, `[]` at :249. Consumers reading `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` now get undefined; collective payloads additionally disclose every host's externalId (usually an email), credentialId, integration and userId where one was disclosed before.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:756-762 — the new catch rethrows `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError.message` as a 400 to an unauthenticated caller; Prisma strings embed model/field names and sometimes argument values. Previously a generic 500.

handleNewBooking.ts:992/1077 dynamic group-booking fan-out: flagged as potentially writing booker-controlled titles into every listed user's calendar. Depends on whether @calcom/lib/defaultEvents marks dynamic events COLLECTIVE — that file is absent from this checkout, so this is unverified. Worth confirming upstream.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:249 logs the full calEvent (attendee PII) and :285 logs the full credential including the encrypted key. VERIFIED IDENTICAL at base commit d7c2e67 — this diff only reindents :249. The new per-destination loop does make :249 fire once per host per booking, widening an existing exposure.

credentialId is the wrong key — it is not unique per destination calendar. One Google/O365 credential backs many calendars, and eventType.destinationCalendar and user.destinationCalendar are independent rows that can share a credential. Nothing dedupes the array at handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1078. Two entries sharing a credentialId → `.find()` returns the first both times → two events in the SAME calendar, while the second reference stores the OTHER externalId → subsequent update/delete 404s. The correct key is the (credentialId, externalId) pair, which CalendarManager.createEvent already has in hand.

CalendarManager.createEvent already receives `externalId` (CalendarManager.ts:221) and does not pass it down — it passes `credentialId` instead, forcing every calendar service to re-derive "which of my calendars does this credential own." Passing the resolved externalId would have fixed all four implementations with zero per-app changes. The resolution logic is currently re-derived ad hoc in five places.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:358 and :530 — `appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug` yields a slug ("google-calendar"), while the constructor at :80 builds `appName: app.name` ("Google Calendar"). VERIFIED both. The same field carries two value spaces depending on which path found the credential, and it flows into EventResult.appName → AppsStatus → booking metadata and error emails. The two DB-fallback blocks are also byte-identical duplicates.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-383 — N+1 plus serialized external calls on the synchronous booking POST. Co-host credentials are never in `calendarCredentials` (built from one user), so the DB fallback fires for every co-host on every booking, followed by N sequential Google/Graph round-trips. The base code used Promise.all for the multi-credential path. No memoization, so a repeated credentialId is refetched.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423-470 — the legacy no-credentialId branch AND the recurring-cancel block were moved inside the new per-reference loop, so cost becomes O(references × credentials × remainingBookings) sequential deleteEvent calls (e.g. 312 API calls where it was 104 for a 3-host weekly collective with 52 occurrences).

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null` on an optional property gives three encodings of "absent" (undefined | null | []), and the diff uses all three. Consumers check inconsistently: `&& length > 0` at EventManager.ts:338, a ternary at googlecalendar:100, a bare `?? []` at office365:73. The "main host is element 0" rule is a positional convention encoded nowhere — no named type, no helper — and `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...` is copy-pasted across ~10 sites in three different spellings.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:689 — `SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` replaced with `["COLLECTIVE","ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(...)`, and :992/:1077 use the "COLLECTIVE" literal while :805 still uses `SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN`. The same discriminator is now both enum-typed and stringly-typed in one file, losing exhaustiveness checking. (Note: the literal at :1021 is PRE-EXISTING — verified at base — so only the 689/992/1077 sites are new drift.)

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 + handleNewBooking.ts:1074 — `schedulingType` added to the exported CalendarEvent interface and populated, but nothing reads `evt.schedulingType`. New surface on a widely-implemented public type with no consumer, and it now joins the serialized webhook payload. (Zero-consumer claim is bounded by the sparse checkout.)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:724-762 — loadUsers fully rewritten, none of it required by the array change: (a) `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` DROPPED from the dynamic-user select while IsFixedAwareUser:355 still declares it required and :869 casts `users as IsFixedAwareUser[]`, so the cast now lies and getBookerUrl(organizerUser) degrades for dynamic bookings; (b) the two new `throw new Error(...)` guards are VERIFIED unreachable as written — a plain Error is neither HttpError nor PrismaClientKnownRequestError, so both messages are discarded and become a generic 500; (c) empty dynamicUserList now throws instead of returning []; (d) `eventType.users || []` fallback dropped; (e) the `// Don't leak to client` guardrail comment deleted (traced: credentials do not reach the response, so a lost comment, not a leak).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592-595 — `console.error(message)` deleted from the catch. VERIFIED the `message` string is still built and then discarded; calendar update failures are now silent. Unrelated to the array refactor.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:191-215 — credentialsMap is keyed by type from getUsersCredentials(user.id) (requesting user only) and applied to every _calendar reference, so a collective reschedule deletes host B's event with the organizer's credential → 404 → the old slot stays blocked. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING logic; the diff touched line 239-241 but did not extend this flow, so it is an uncovered flow rather than an introduced regression.
packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — user-visible string change "Notes have been hidden by the organiser" → "organizer", written into calendar event bodies attendees see. Unrelated.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:996-997 — `firstName: ""` / `lastName: ""` added to team-member objects; TeamMember (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:40-45) has no such fields. Inert, unrelated.

Cosmetic churn unrelated to the fix: handleNewBooking.ts:370/383 `orginalBookingDuration` → `originalBookingDuration`; handleCancelBooking.ts:474 "behaviour" → "behavior"; packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/builder.ts:1-2 import split.

Leftover debris: googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145-146 orphaned comment plus stray blank line; EventManager.ts:117 `@NOTE` comment that reads as a design decision but annotates the line that crashes on an empty array; handleCancelBooking.ts:418 `bookingCalendarReference` keeps its singular name after becoming a filter() result.

Zero test coverage for the new behavior. No *.test.ts / *.spec.ts / __tests__ exist in any touched package; the sole test-side change is one fixture line at apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249. Nothing exercises >1 destination calendar, credentialId matching in createAllCalendarEvents, the new DB-credential fallback, an empty/null array, or a collective booking end-to-end. Given that the highest-severity defects above are all mechanical [0]/matching errors, this is the omission that let them through.

Bottom line:** the change is not done. Beyond the two unconditional crashes (`EventManager.ts:118`, undefined `credential` at `:512`) and the unrelated inverted boolean in `create.handler.ts:151`, the core intent is not delivered — `credentialId` matching landed only in the Google service, the CalDAV base returns silent false success, and the confirm/payment/reschedule paths still build one-element arrays. My recommendation matches the scaffold's `NEEDS_REVISION`.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is a meta “scope caveat” about the reviewer’s limited checkout (missing schema.prisma/node_modules/other files) and inability to run tsc. It does not identify any bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff itself, nor is it a verifiable problem in the changed code.

adjudication.rationale: The cited TODO comment (`// TODO: i18n this string?`) is not introduced or modified in substance by this diff; the only change on that line is the string spelling from "organiser" to "organizer" while the TODO marker remains unchanged. Also, leaving an existing TODO comment is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Manifest blocker: "missing shard result for shard-01" — no reviewer output was recorded for the single shard covering all 23 paths; scaffold verdict NEEDS_REVISION.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is about review/CI infrastructure (“missing shard result for shard-01”, “no reviewer output recorded”, “scaffold verdict NEEDS_REVISION”), not about a code defect introduced by the diff. Nothing in the provided code changes can be used to verify whether a shard result is missing or whether reviewer output was recorded, so this is not a verifiable problem present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PASS (0 blocking) — contradicted by the security lens below; the gate did not detect the removed credential-ownership checks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new code paths that, when a `credentialId` is present but not found in the in-memory `this.calendarCredentials` / `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, will fetch an arbitrary credential directly from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: ... } })` (see `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, `EventManager.updateBooking`, and `handleCancelBooking`). These lookups are not scoped/validated against the current user/team (no `userId`/`teamId` check), which effectively removes the prior implicit ownership constraint of “only use credentials already associated with this user/session” and can enable using a credential by ID alone if that ID is ever attacker-influenced. This is a real, verifiable security/correctness regression present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PASS (0 blocking) — contradicted by the completeness lens; the only test-side change is one Playwright fixture line.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding does not identify a specific defect introduced by the code changes; it’s a meta comment about review “completeness” and notes that only one Playwright fixture line changed. While it’s true the diff contains major production changes with minimal test updates (only the Playwright expectation changes from null to []), that is not a directly verifiable bug/correctness issue in the diff itself—just a subjective test-coverage concern.

These lookups are unscoped (no `userId`/`teamId`/ownership predicate) and then the returned credential fields (including `key`, `userId`, `teamId`, `invalid`) are used to construct a credential object and proceed with calendar operations. Previously, the code only used `this.calendarCredentials` / `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, which implicitly constrained credentials to the relevant user/team.
